answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can tie identity to satellite laser telemetry. A node tracks an orbiting beacon at its zenith transit, passing downlink photons through a prism to log arrival jitter inside a secure hardware kernel. An attacker must maintain discrete, steerable optical transceivers per identity, incurring steep hardware and site-licensing costs. However, cloud cover and dense fog scatter the optical beam, causing intermittent authentication outages.
